title: D1-04 Refund State Machine Candidate

x-luckread.note: Only exact, signature-verified Hyperswitch refund_details resources may advance persisted provider state; create API responses may set the initial reservation's first provider observation but signed webhooks remain the asynchronous lifecycle authority.

x-transitions.precondition: An owner-scoped refund reservation exists in D1-04 with a stable refund_id, customer-scoped idempotency key and immutable payment/amount/currency snapshot; the Hyperswitch response matches the snapshot.
Exact signed refund_details webhook or matching create-refund response identifies the same refund_id, payment_id, merchant, amount and currency.
Exact signed refund_details webhook or matching provider response confirms succeeded; the resource timestamp is valid and local version CAS succeeds.
Exact signed refund_details webhook or matching provider response confirms failed; the resource timestamp is valid and local version CAS succeeds.
A newer, matching signed refund_details event or same-state provider observation is bound to the local refund and passes version CAS.
A newer, matching signed refund_review event confirms manual/connector review.
A newer, matching signed refund_succeeded event confirms provider refund success.
A newer, matching signed refund_failed event confirms provider refund failure.
A newer matching signed refund_review event confirms the refund remains under review.
A newer matching signed refund_succeeded event confirms final success.
A newer matching signed refund_failed event confirms final failure.
Exact duplicate observation only; no new financial mutation is applied. A succeeded refund is terminal.
Exact duplicate observation only; no new financial mutation is applied. A failed refund is terminal.

x-global-guards: Every refund is bound to the authenticated customer, original payment, provider and merchant; client-supplied owner IDs are never trusted.
A stable refund_id and customer-scoped idempotency key identify one semantic refund request; key reuse with a changed payment, amount, currency or reason conflicts.
Refund amounts use integer minor units; local active reservations cannot exceed the payment amount and Hyperswitch independently enforces actual amount_captured.
INITIATING, pending, review and succeeded amounts remain reserved. Failed refunds release the reserved amount.
Every state update requires version = current_version + 1 and a strictly increasing canonical provider_updated_at; stale or invalid timestamps require reconciliation.
A webhook receipt can apply only when event type, refund_id, payment_id, merchant_id, amount and currency match the immutable local snapshot and signature verification succeeds.
Same provider/merchant/event_id and same payload hash is an idempotent replay; same event identity with a different hash creates a conflict record and cannot overwrite the first receipt.
Refund state is not a Ledger entry, wallet balance mutation or subscription-entitlement transition. Financial posting and D1-01 entitlement changes require separate authorized workflows.

x-failure-semantics.providerTimeout: Keep the durable INITIATING reservation; retry with the same refund_id and idempotency key.
x-failure-semantics.providerReview: Persist review; keep the amount reserved.
x-failure-semantics.providerFailure: Persist failed; release the local refund reservation without deleting the request.
x-failure-semantics.webhookPayloadConflict: Retain first receipt and record conflict; no refund transition.
